title: Canonical Header Count Seam
statement: For every machine format $F$, there exist a finite Turing machine $C$ over the Boolean alphabet, a work-tape index $d$ whose index is $1$, entry and exit states, and a constant $a\\in\\mathbb N$. For every Boolean input $\\alpha$, at some time $t\\le a(|\\alpha|+1)$ the machine reaches the exit state with the canonical header of $\\alpha$ on tape zero, its fixed-width increment (with overflow replaced by the empty word) on tape $d$, and empty words on all other tapes; at every earlier time $u<t$ its state is not the exit state.
hypotheses_covered: no earlier visit to the exit state
final tape words are the canonical header updated at tape 1 by its fixed-width increment, with overflow represented by empty word
